title: account channel — schema-first (AFB backend<->AFB frontend only; not part of afb.execution.v1 wire)
description: Negotiated via auth.support/auth_ok.support (capability id afbws.account.channel.v2). Same convention as afbws.alarm.v2/afbws.market: ONE schema id per message (`afbws.account.<op>.v2`, no .request/.response/.push suffixes); the same schema is the request, its response (echoes `request_id`) and, for `list`/`orders`, the server push (a message WITHOUT `request_id`). `events` has no push; `error` is the single typed error. Operations: list, orders, events, cash, set, delete, reconcile, ledger, error. `list` takes `bf_id` + `account_id`. ACCOUNT ID. `account_id` is the id of the `account` row in trading.db (`account-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx`) for a `virtual` and a broker account; for a `bond` account (virtual account of a bond portfolio; created and deleted together with the portfolio) it is `account-<suffix>` (the portfolio id `portfolio-<suffix>` with the prefix replaced). A broker account of a connector is registered by the backend when the connector reports it; its number at the broker is `external_id` of the snapshot. Only the trading account of a connector is listed. `bf_id` is the account type for AFB-side accounts: `virtual` (trading simulation) and `bond` (portfolio account). The lifecycle of a `virtual` account is `set` (open / rename / reopen) and `delete` (physical removal without history, otherwise closing); the lifecycle of a `bond` account is bound to its portfolio (afbws.bonds.channel.v1), so there is no `open` for it; target quantities of a `bond` account are set by afbws.bonds.positions.set.v1. Operations `cash`, `reconcile`, `ledger` serve accounts of type `bond` (the backend answers `not_supported` for other types); each has no server push, so `request_id` is always required. The money of a `bond` account is held ONLY in its base currency: cash[] has at most one element. Every account snapshot carries `lifecycle` (`active | suspended | closed`): `suspended` and `closed` accounts stay in `list`; `closed` is read-only, a closed account of the user may be reopened by `set` with `lifecycle: active`. `items` are explicit allow-list projections built by backend/trade/public_views.py (never a verbatim proxy of a BF broker.* payload); $defs accountSnapshot/order/eventRecord are this file's own strict shapes, reusing only the field-level $defs of payloads/broker.accounts.json. A multi-currency account (broker / virtual) is expressed through cash[] (one entry per currency); the virtual account fills `as_of`. `account` means a single account (one bf_id may have more than one), not the connector itself.

bfId.description: Connector id (broker `bf_id`) or the type of an AFB-side account: `virtual`, `bond`. Open string: new account types need no schema change.

accountId.description: Id of the `account` row in trading.db (`account-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx`) for `virtual` and broker accounts; for a `bond` account — `account-<suffix>` (the portfolio id `portfolio-<suffix>` with the prefix replaced).

position.title: Public position projection built by AFB (backend/trade/public_views.py). Own definition, independent of payloads/broker.accounts.json#/$defs/position: BF positions carry only broker_ref {broker, symbol}; AFB restores the optional `instrument` block itself (from its catalog / finam.db).

instrument.description: Instrument block restored by AFB; optional.

instrument_key.description: Catalog instrument key (`MISX:<board>:<secid>`, case-sensitive). Filled by AFB-side accounts (`bond`); optional for broker positions.

accrued_int.description: Accrued coupon interest per unit in the instrument currency (a bond position); null/absent when not applicable.

accountOp.title: One entry of the account operation log (facts only; written by the backend only).
accountOp.description: A light journal of facts: rows are independent (no ids, no links between rows). Decimal strings for money and prices. ALL account money is in the account base currency, so `amount` is always in the base currency; the instrument currency appears only in `price` / `accrued_int` and, when it differs from the base one, in `fx_currency` / `fx_rate`. No spread and no fees. `kind`: deposit | withdraw (user cash movement), buy | sell (emulated at LAST MOEX, by a quantity edit or an auto-sale), coupon | amortization | redemption (income credited by the schedule), reconcile (manual or broker-sync correction, written by `afbws.account.reconcile.v2`: a position row has the NEW quantity / average price and amount 0; a cash row has no instrument_key and `amount` = new balance minus the previous one).

ts.description: ISO 8601 UTC time of the record; for an income row, the time it was credited.

amount.description: Signed cash movement in the account BASE currency, decimal string: negative for buy / withdraw, positive for the rest. For a reconcile cash row it is the correction (new balance minus the previous one); for a reconcile position row it is 0.

instrument_key.description: Instrument key. Present for buy / sell / coupon / amortization / redemption / reconcile; absent for deposit / withdraw.

quantity.description: Number of units. Present together with instrument_key; for income rows it is the quantity held at the moment of crediting; for a reconcile row it is the NEW quantity of the position (a reference point, not a delta).

price.description: buy / sell / reconcile (position row) only: clean price per unit in the INSTRUMENT currency (decimal string); for reconcile it is the new average price.

accrued_int.description: buy / sell / reconcile (position row) only: accrued interest per unit in the INSTRUMENT currency (decimal string); for reconcile it is the new average accrued interest.

event_date.description: coupon / amortization / redemption only: YYYY-MM-DD payment date by the schedule (used to match the row with the schedule).

fx_currency.description: Present only if the instrument currency differs from the account base currency: the currency the amount was converted from / to (for a reconcile row that opens a new position — the instrument currency).

fx_rate.description: Present together with fx_currency: base-currency units per 1 unit of fx_currency (CETS LAST, decimal string). The amount in the instrument currency is amount / fx_rate (informational for a reconcile row: its amount is 0).

accountSnapshot.title: One broker account's public projection — see backend/trade/public_views.py::account_snapshot(). Never carries broker_account_id (see payloads/broker.accounts.json — the same field the wire type deliberately dropped).

account_id.description: Id of the `account` row in trading.db (`account-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx`) for `virtual` and broker accounts; `account-<suffix>` (the portfolio id `portfolio-<suffix>` with the prefix replaced) for a `bond` account.

kind.description: Account kind: `virtual` (trading simulation), `bond` (portfolio account), `broker` (the trading account of a broker connector).

name.description: Display name: the account name for `virtual`, the portfolio name for `bond`; null for a broker account.

external_id.description: Broker accounts only: the account number at the broker (as reported by the connector); null for `virtual` and `bond`.

lifecycle.description: Account life state. `active`: normal operation (deals are published to it, money moves, it is offered when choosing an account for a plan). `suspended`: set by the system when the source does not confirm the account (a broker account: the connector's report has no such account, or the connector was removed; a bond account: the portfolio is unavailable); reverts to `active` automatically when the source confirms it again; while suspended, publishing / moving a deal to the account and money operations are forbidden. `closed`: closed by the user (`account.delete` of an account with history) or, for a bond account, by the system when the portfolio is deleted; read-only, the whole history stays available; the user may reopen an account closed by the user (`account.set` with `lifecycle: active`), an account closed by the system is not reopened by the user. `closed`/`suspended` accounts stay in `account.list`.

tradable.description: True for the account orders are placed on. Only the trading account of a connector is listed, so it is true for every broker account; always true for `virtual` and `bond`.

readonly.description: Broker / virtual accounts only (every `bf_id` except `bond`; required there, forbidden for `bond`).

owner.description: `bf_id: bond` only (required there, forbidden for other accounts). Owner of the portfolio account. An EMPTY object `{}` means the account is the caller's own. For a public account of somebody else (read-only for the caller) `name` and `tier` describe the owner; `null` means the owner is unknown.

name.description: Display name of the owner; null — unknown. Absent for the caller's own account.

tier.description: Tier of the owner (e.g. `admin`, `manager`); null — unknown. Absent for the caller's own account.

cash.description: Cash balances, one entry per currency. For `bf_id: bond` account money is held ONLY in the account base currency: at most one element.

order.title: Allow-list projection over payloads/broker.orders.json#/$defs/order plus AFB/frontend-synthesized display fields (client_order_id, cancel_source) that BF never sends — see accountStore.ts::normalizeOrder. `symbol` is not part of the BF wire shape either; it stays optional and is resolved by the frontend from the owning deal when present.

eventRecord.title: Journal of incoming BF events (JSONL direction=in) for one bf_id/day — unchanged from the legacy account/get_events response. See ExecutionService.get_account_events_for_user and event_translator.envelope_to_event_record.

list.title: afbws.account.list.v2 — read accounts (request / response / server push).
list.description: Request (`request_id`, no `items`): optional `bf_id` (only that connector's accounts; omitted = every account of every accessible connector), optional `account_id` (a single account; use together with `bf_id`), optional `force` (bypass the cached BfRuntimeState.accounts snapshot and re-fetch from BF). Response (same `request_id`, with `items`): only `request_id` + `items[]` (accountSnapshot, possibly empty; each carries `lifecycle`, closed and suspended accounts included). Push (no `request_id`, server-initiated): the full account list of ONE `bf_id` — `bf_id`, `items[]` (BF's broker.accounts is a full snapshot, never a delta; the virtual accounts are pushed the same way). Only the trading account of a connector is listed. For `bf_id: "bond"` (accounts of bond portfolios, `account_id` = `account-<suffix>` (the portfolio id `portfolio-<suffix>` with the prefix replaced)): a request without `account_id` returns only the caller's own accounts; with `account_id` the caller's own or a readable public one (staff accounts are `visibility public`, read-only for others). A `bond` snapshot carries `owner` instead of `readonly`: `{}` for the caller's own account, `{name, tier}` of the owner (null when unknown) for somebody else's public one; broker and virtual snapshots carry `readonly` and no `owner`. The snapshot is filled from the account log: `cash[]` per currency, `equity` in the base currency (cash + market value), `tradable: true`, `status: ok`, positions carry `instrument_key` and `accrued_int`. The push for `bond` is event-driven (after `cash`, a quantity edit, an income credit, a composition change), like the virtual account. A request carrying `items` or a response/push carrying request-only fields is invalid.

force.description: Request only: bypass the cached accounts snapshot and re-fetch from BF.

orders.title: afbws.account.orders.v2 — orders of one account (request / response / server push).
orders.description: Request (`request_id`, no `items`): `bf_id` required; `account_id` omitted = the connector's default (trading) account (the only account order history is available for, see payloads/broker.orders.json). Response (same `request_id`, with `items`): `bf_id`, `account_id`, `items[]`. Push (no `request_id`, server-initiated): `bf_id`, `account_id`, `items[]` for the default (trading) account.

events.title: afbws.account.events.v2 — journal of incoming BF events for one bf_id/day (request / response).
events.description: Request (`request_id`, no `items`): `bf_id` required, `date` (YYYY-MM-DD market date) omitted = today (market_today()), `account_id` optional (only the events of this one account). Response (same `request_id`, with `items`): `bf_id`, `date`, `items[]`. There is NO server push for events: `request_id` is always required.

account_id.description: Optional filter: only the events of this account. Request only.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD market date; omitted in a request means today (market_today()).

cash.title: afbws.account.cash.v2 — deposit or withdraw cash of a `bond` account (request / response).
cash.description: Request: `account_id`, `kind` (deposit | withdraw), `currency`, `amount` (positive decimal string). Account money is held only in the account base currency: `currency` must equal it, otherwise the error is `validation_error`. The backend writes a `deposit` / `withdraw` operation (amount in the base currency); the starting capital is the first deposit. Response (same `request_id`, with `item`): the updated account snapshot. Errors (`afbws.account.error.v2`): `insufficient_cash` (withdraw above the balance), `validation_error` (`currency` differs from the account base currency), `forbidden` (not the owner / not staff for a public account), `not_found`, `not_supported`. No server push (the owner receives `afbws.account.list.v2`).

currency.description: Request only: must equal the account base currency.

set.title: afbws.account.set.v2 — open, rename or reopen a virtual account (request / response).
set.description: Lifecycle of a `virtual` account. Request: `name` (1..64 characters, unique among the owner's NOT closed virtual accounts, case-insensitive) and, optionally, `account_id`. WITHOUT `account_id` the request opens a new virtual account: `amount` is required (starting capital in rubles, a positive decimal string, no upper bound); `lifecycle` is forbidden. WITH `account_id` it renames that account: `amount` is forbidden. WITH `account_id` and `lifecycle: active` it REOPENS the caller's own closed account (`closed -> active`); `amount` is forbidden, `name` is then optional (omitted = keep the name; the name must stay unique among the owner's not closed accounts, otherwise `validation_error`). The limit of virtual accounts counts only not closed accounts (reopening over the limit is `limit_exceeded`). Renaming a closed account is not allowed (`conflict`: reopen it first); reopening an account that is not closed is `conflict`. An account closed by the system (a portfolio account) is not reopened by the user: `forbidden`. Response (same `request_id`): `item` — the account snapshot after the change. Errors (`afbws.account.error.v2`): `validation_error` (bad or duplicate `name`, bad `amount`), `not_found` (unknown or foreign `account_id`), `conflict` (rename of a closed account / reopen of a not closed one), `forbidden` (reopen of an account closed by the system), `limit_exceeded` (the limit of virtual accounts is reached), `not_supported` (the account is not a `virtual` one). No server push (the owner receives `afbws.account.list.v2`).

account_id.description: Request only: absent — open a new account, present — rename it (or reopen it together with `lifecycle: active`).

name.description: Request only: account name, unique among the owner's virtual accounts, case-insensitive.

amount.description: Request only, opening only: starting capital in rubles, a positive decimal string, no upper bound.

lifecycle.description: Request only: reopen the caller's own closed account (`closed -> active`). Allowed only together with `account_id`; forbidden when opening a new account and together with `amount`.

delete.title: afbws.account.delete.v2 — delete or close a virtual account (request / response).
delete.description: Request: `account_id` of a `virtual` account. An account without history (no deals, trades, cash flows or adjustments; hidden deals count) is deleted physically. An account with history is CLOSED instead (`lifecycle: closed`; read-only, the history stays available, the user may reopen it with `account.set`). Closing while the account has live deals (`published | active | paused`) is `conflict`. The last virtual account can be deleted too. Response (same `request_id`): `account_id` of the deleted or closed account (the shape does not tell which; a closed account stays in `afbws.account.list.v2` with `lifecycle: closed`). Errors (`afbws.account.error.v2`): `not_found` (unknown or foreign), `not_supported` (the account is not a `virtual` one), `conflict` (the account has live deals). No server push (the owner receives `afbws.account.list.v2`).

reconcile.title: afbws.account.reconcile.v2 — reconcile a `bond` account with the real state (request / response).
reconcile.description: Serves `bond` accounts only; for a `virtual` (and broker) account the backend answers `not_supported`. Manual (later also broker / report) correction of positions and free cash. Request: `account_id`, `positions[]` (0..200, TARGET state of each instrument) and/or `cash` (TARGET free-cash balance in the account base currency); at least one of a non-empty `positions` or `cash`. The values are absolute: the backend computes the difference from the current state and skips unchanged rows (idempotent). A position row writes one `reconcile` log row with the NEW quantity / average price (amount 0; quantity 0 closes the position); a `cash` row writes one `reconcile` row with amount = new balance minus the previous one. Each position row is executed separately, partial success is allowed. Response (same `request_id`): `item` — the account snapshot after the edit — and `rejected[]` (refused position rows with `reason`; empty when all went through). A whole-request failure (including a negative `cash`) is `afbws.account.error.v2`. No server push.

quantity.description: New quantity (not a delta); 0 closes the position.

avg_price.description: New average clean price per unit in the INSTRUMENT currency (decimal string, like `average_price` of the snapshot). Required when the position does not exist yet and quantity > 0; absent for an existing position — the price is kept.

accrued_int.description: New average accrued interest per unit in the INSTRUMENT currency (decimal string); null — unknown; absent — keep the current value.

cash.description: Request only: new free-cash balance in the account BASE currency (decimal string, >= 0). Absent — cash is not changed.

reason.description: no_fx: no exchange rate for a new position in a foreign currency; not_in_set: the instrument is not in the portfolio composition; not_supported: instrument class has no provider; invalid_value: a new position without `avg_price` or a malformed number; forbidden: not allowed for the caller.

ledger.title: afbws.account.ledger.v2 — page of the account operation log (request / response).
ledger.description: Request: `account_id`, optional `before` (opaque cursor string taken from a previous response `next`: return entries older than it), optional `limit` (1..200). Entries are returned newest first (new -> old). Response (same `request_id`, with `items`): `account_id`, `items[]` (accountOp), `next` — the opaque cursor to pass as `before` for the next page, or null at the end. The client must not parse or construct cursors. No server push.

before.description: Request only. Opaque cursor from a previous response `next`.

error.title: afbws.account.error.v2 — typed error for a whole request (server -> client).

code.description: The common error codes plus `insufficient_cash` (account.cash withdraw above the balance) and `limit_exceeded` (account.set: the limit of virtual accounts is reached). `forbidden`, `not_found`, `conflict` and `not_supported` are common codes.
